The outputs asserted in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts match exactly the strings produced by ANNOTATION + the insertion logic.
3) Implementation of @story format auto-fix (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT / REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE / REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE): - Rule: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Multiple functions are annotated with `@story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md` and `@req REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT`. - `meta.fixable: "code"` with comment: "fixable support is limited to safe @story path suffix normalization per Story 008.0". - `validateStoryAnnotation(...)` logic: - If the current value already matches `pathPattern`, it returns (no error, no fix). - If the value contains whitespace, it calls `reportInvalidStoryFormat(...)` (error only, no fix). - Otherwise, it calls `getFixedStoryPath(collapsed)`. - If `fixed` is non-null and matches `pathPattern`, it calls `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(context, comment, collapsed, fixed)` to attach a fix. - If not, it falls back to `reportInvalidStoryFormat(...)` (error without fix). - Safe replacement helpers: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts - `getFixedStoryPath(original)` (annotated with Story 008.0 and REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT / SAFE / PRESERVE): - Returns null (no fix) if `original` contains `".."` (directory traversal) or already ends with `.story.md`. - If it ends with `.story`, returns `${original}.md`. - If it ends with `.md` (but not `.story.md`), replaces it with `.story.md`. - Otherwise appends `.story.md`. - Only the suffix is changed; the base path is preserved. - `createStoryFix(...)` in valid-annotation-format.ts: - Uses `sourceCode.getText(comment)` and regex to locate only the value portion of the `@story` tag. - Computes a `[start, end]` range over the value substring and returns a fixer that calls `fixer.replaceTextRange(fixRange, fixed)`. - If it cannot safely locate this substring, returns null, which causes a non-fixing error path instead. - These behaviors align with tests: - `adds .md extension for .story path` and `adds .story.md extension when missing entirely` pass, and `already-correct story path is unchanged` is also validated.
4) Error handling and safety: - Missing @story annotations: - `hasStoryAnnotation(...)` uses JSDoc, preceding comments, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, and fallbackTextBeforeHasStory, all wrapped in try/catch to avoid crashes and to skip auto-fix when detection fails. - If any heuristic finds `@story`, no report or fix is emitted (prevents duplicate annotations). - Invalid @story formats: - Auto-fix is only attached when `getFixedStoryPath(...)` returns a non-null path that satisfies the configured regex; otherwise only an error is reported. - Paths with traversal (`..`) and already-correct `.story.md` are explicitly skipped (`null` from getFixedStoryPath) so no fix is attempted. - This matches the acceptance criterion that edge cases are handled gracefully and unfixable/ambiguous cases do not receive auto-fixes.
5) Documentation of auto-fix behavior: - user-docs/api-reference.md documents the behavior for both relevant rules: - `traceability/require-story-annotation`: - Describes that when run with `--fix`, the rule inserts a single-line placeholder JSDoc @story annotation above missing functions, methods, TS declare functions, and TS interface method signatures. - States that this template is currently fixed but structured for future configurability and that fixes do not alter function bodies or runtime behavior, matching REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE, and REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE. - Notes that selective enabling of different auto-fix behaviors is planned, not yet implemented, in line with REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE being marked "Not yet implemented" in the story. - `traceability/valid-annotation-format`: - Describes suffix-only auto-fix behavior for `@story` paths (adding `.md` to `.story`, or `.story.md` when no extension) implemented via `getFixedStoryPath` and `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix`. - Explicitly states it does not change directories, infer new names, or alter surrounding comment text/whitespace, again matching REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT, SAFE, and PRESERVE.
6) Scope alignment with the story: - The story itself marks REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE as "Not yet implemented" and clarifies that this iteration only covers: - Auto-adding @story annotations with a simple built-in template. - Simple, safe suffix normalization of @story paths. - The code and docs match exactly that scope: there is a fixed template and no configuration for templates or selective fix types yet, while the implemented fixes are conservative and fully tested. - All Jest tests, including the ones directly tied to this story, pass successfully.
traceability.notes: All in-scope acceptance criteria for docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md are implemented and verified. ESLint --fix integrates correctly for (1) inserting missing @story annotations on functions/methods/TS signatures via the require-story-annotation rule and its helpers, and (2) performing safe, minimal @story path suffix normalization via the valid-annotation-format rule and getFixedStoryPath/createStoryFix. The behavior is covered by dedicated tests in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts (and supporting rule tests), which all pass. Error handling is conservative: fixes are omitted when detection is ambiguous or unsafe, and only clearly safe suffix changes are applied. User-facing documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md accurately describes these auto-fix capabilities and explicitly calls out future, not-yet-implemented enhancements (configurable templates and selective fix toggles), consistent with the story’s own notes. Therefore, the story is fully satisfied for this iteration.
